definition.name: Independent thermal cut-out
definition.description: A separate safety contact opens when the illustrative limit is exceeded.

terminals.label: COM
terminals.purpose: Common fed contact, paired with OUT. The independent thermal limit latches the pair open after its declared limit is exceeded; reset after restoring an acceptable temperature. This contact does not produce its own supply.

terminals.label: OUT
terminals.purpose: Controlled output contact, paired with COM. The independent thermal limit latches the pair open after its declared limit is exceeded; reset after restoring an acceptable temperature. This contact does not produce its own supply.

parts.name: Housing
parts.purpose: The enclosure supports and separates functional parts. This original teaching model is representative equipment, not a manufacturer drawing.

parts.name: Removable cover
parts.purpose: The cover limits access to internal connections. Opening it here is a virtual inspection operation.

parts.name: Terminal clamps
parts.purpose: Metal clamps establish connections to individual conductors. The circuit engine connects terminal IDs, not the apparent proximity of 3D wires.

parts.name: Mounting and fixings
parts.purpose: Mounting hardware supports the equipment. Screws, rail clips and glands are modelled separately from electrical connections.

parts.name: Thermal protection
parts.purpose: A thermal element responds to heating or sustained excess current. Timing is illustrative here; it is not a manufacturer trip curve.

parts.name: Switching contacts
parts.purpose: Contacts either connect or separate their terminal pairs. Their position is linked to the simulation state, including normally open and normally closed functions.
